markdown_content: ## Points of Measure (POM): Where to Find and Organize Them This section explains what Points of Measure (POMs) are in CLO, where to access them, and how to organize POMs using folders and import/export options. In CLO, **Points of Measure** are also called **POMs**. They appear in the UI like **rulers/comb-like guides** with measurement lines. To view and manage them, open the **Object Browser** and look for the **Points of Measure** tab (the ruler/comb icon). You can **organize POMs into folders**. For example, you can create folders such as: - **Front** - **Back** - **Body Sleeve** - **Totals** You can also **open and bring in** existing measurement tables (e.g., a whole set of POMs). If you save your POM setup, you can save **2D and 3D lines**, and export the POM data as **CSV** files. After saving, you can **re-open** the saved file and the full POM list will be available. From there, you can select a POM and add it to your model. --- ## Creating POM Lines: Polyline vs Segment Line This section covers how to create POM guides and the two line creation modes: **polyline** and **segment line**. It also includes keyboard shortcuts and how segments follow existing geometry. When creating POMs, there are **two options** for line creation: 1. **Polyline (current mode)** - Click anywhere to place points. - **Double-click** to end the line. - Hold **Shift** to keep guidelines straight (recommended for precision). - Double-click to end. 2. **Segment Line** - Press **P** once on the keyboard to switch to **segment lines**. - The segment line **follows segment behavior** (i.e., it follows along the segment structure). - **Double-click** to end and finalize the pre-set line behavior. Once created, you can **double-click and rename** POMs. POMs can include guided measurement paths (the transcript notes a “**700 code**” behavior as part of how the preset line works). --- ## POM Calculator Notepad: Add/Subtract and Save Results This section explains the new **POM calculator notepad** workflow for performing arithmetic directly on POM-related measurements and saving results back into totals. A key update is the ability to **add or subtract POM measurements** and see the **difference** without using external tools. CLO provides a dedicated **calculator notepad**. ### How to open the Calculator Notepad - Go to the **top toolbar** - Select **2D** - Choose **Calculator Notepad** This opens the notepad and shows prior calculations for the current work file. You can also manage calculations in **groups** (for example, create groups like “front/back/center” and organize totals). ### Using the POM calculator When you click a calculator within the interface, it opens a **POM calculator** where you can enter math such as: - Example entered: **95 − 35** - Press **Equal** - Click **Apply** to push the result into the **POM total** (the first/active target total) You can delete unwanted entries (e.g., using **Delete**) and re-run calculations as needed. ### Minimizing and workflow The transcript shows that you can minimize the notepad and calculator windows while continuing work, then return to review or apply results. --- ## Applying Calculated POMs: Updating, Drag/Drop, and Clearing This section describes how to insert calculations into POM totals, how to clear and re-import values, and how updates propagate (including a limitation). ### Clearing and importing values - Press **C** on the keyboard to **clear** calculations/inputs. - Press **C** again as needed to clear previously entered math. - To bring in values from the report/POM list, press **C**, then select the **calculator next to it** to insert the value. ### Example: combining armhole measurements The workflow demonstrated: 1. Click the **front armhole** value (example shown: **8.609**). 2. Click the **back armhole** value and add it. 3. Use **Equal**, then **Apply**. 4. The result becomes a **new POM** representing that calculation. 5. You can **drag and drop** it into the **total** so it contributes to overall grading. ### Grading visibility The transcript notes that the result includes **grading** information and that grading can be viewed via **dropdowns** inside the calculator notepad area. ### Update behavior limitation (important) If you **change the pattern**, the corresponding POM values change as well. However, the transcript highlights a limitation: - After pattern changes, the calculated POM may **not automatically update** in the target area. - To refresh: - Click **Update** in the calculator notepad to update the calculation. - If the updated value does not reflect in the target list, you may need to **delete and reapply** the calculated POM. --- ## Correct POM Math: Parentheses, Differences, and Ease Calculations This section shows how to perform correct arithmetic for POM-derived measurements, emphasizing **parentheses** and using results to compute differences (e.g., ease between armhole and sleeve cap). ### Parentheses rules When entering math: - **Parentheses determine evaluation order**. - Anything inside parentheses is calculated first, then operations outside are applied afterward. ### Example: front armhole + back armhole − sleeve cap The transcript demonstrates computing an “ease” style difference: 1. Clear inputs. 2. Add: - **Front armhole + Back armhole** 3. Use **parentheses**: - **(front armhole + back armhole) − sleeve cap** 4. Press **Equal** and then **Apply**. The example result shown is a **0.679** difference, described as the **ease** between the armhole(s) and the sleeve cap. After applying, the generated POM reflects the expression like: - **front armhole + back armhole − sleeve cap** ### Alternative setup (also valid) The transcript also notes another equivalent approach: - Compute the same relationship by subtracting in the opposite order (the result will differ in sign depending on which term is subtracted from which). ### Editing flexibility The calculator supports multiple ways to structure expressions. The key guidance is to set up the equation correctly (especially with parentheses) so the resulting POM calculation matches the intended measurement relationship. --- ## Summary of What You Can Do with the POM Calculator Update This section consolidates the practical capabilities demonstrated: create POMs, compute differences/additions, apply results to totals, view grading, and manage updates. With the **POM calculator notepad**, you can: - Perform **addition/subtraction** of POM measurements directly in CLO - Use **Equal** and **Apply** to create new POMs from calculations - **Drag and drop** calculated POMs into **totals** - View **grading** details in the calculator notepad UI (including via dropdowns) - Clear and re-enter values using **C** - Handle updates with a known limitation: calculated results may require **Update** and sometimes **delete/reapply** after pattern changes
